title: Computer Programming II
description: The CCMAS second programming course: advanced object-oriented programming in Java. It reviews arrays, methods and recursion, then covers classes, objects and constructors, access and non-access modifiers, inheritance and polymorphism, abstraction, interfaces, and exceptions, collections and GUI programming. Built from Dr B. I. Ayinla's COS 202 slides; the exceptions, collections and GUI topic, which has no lecture in the folder, is written from general knowledge following the course outline and the GUI practical assignment.

topics.title: Arrays, Methods and Recursion
topics.summary: COS 202 begins by reviewing arrays (fixed-size, same-type collections stored contiguously, including multi-dimensional arrays), methods with parameters, return values and overloading, and recursion with a base case.

topics.title: Classes, Objects and Constructors
topics.summary: Object-oriented programming builds software from objects that bundle data and behaviour. A class is a blueprint; an object is an instance with state, behaviour and identity, created with new. Constructors initialise objects and can be default, parameterised, copy or private.

topics.title: Access and Non-Access Modifiers
topics.summary: Modifiers set the access level or add other features to classes, attributes, methods and constructors. Access modifiers are public, private, default and protected; non-access modifiers include final, static, abstract, transient, synchronized and volatile.
subtopics: Modifiers for classes: final and abstract

topics.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
topics.summary: Inheritance lets a subclass acquire the fields and methods of a superclass with extends, forming an IS-A relationship. Java supports single, multilevel and hierarchical inheritance with classes, and multiple and hybrid inheritance only through interfaces. Polymorphism lets one method take many forms through overloading and overriding.
subtopics: Multiple and hybrid inheritance through interfaces

topics.title: Abstraction and Encapsulation
topics.summary: Abstraction hides implementation details and shows only essential features, achieved with abstract classes (partial abstraction) and interfaces. Encapsulation wraps data and methods into a class and restricts direct access with private fields and public getters and setters.

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.summary: An interface is a contract that specifies the behaviour a class should provide. A class implements one or more interfaces, which gives Java multiple inheritance of type and dynamic method dispatch. JDK 8 and 9 added default, static and private methods, and functional interfaces with a single abstract method.
subtopics: Functional interfaces, private methods and extending interfaces

topics.title: Exceptions, Collections and GUI Programming
topics.summary: The later part of the course outline covers using the Java API: exceptions and exception handling, the collections List, Stack and Queue with iterators, and event-driven GUI programming with Swing components and event listeners.
